## Product description

# Tools Coveted By Award-winning Creators 

 Pencils, sharpeners and notebooks for writers, artists, composers and anyone who does their best thinking with a pencil in hand. Genuine California Incense-cedar. Japanese graphite. The iconic ferrule that has been our signature for ninety years. 

# Built on Heritage 

 Blackwing's roots go back to the 1930s, when it was the pencil of choice for creators including John Steinbeck and Chuck Jones. The brand disappeared in the 1990s and returned in 2010. Today Blackwing crafts pencils, notebooks and analog tools for people who want to slow down. 

- I'm new to Blackwing. Which pencil should I start with? 

 Most people start with the Pearl - it sits between the soft Matte and the firm 602. To try all four cores before committing to a dozen, the Pencil Essentials Set includes one of each. 
- What do soft, firm, balanced and extra-firm actually mean? 

 They describe how much graphite the pencil lays down and how long it holds a point. Softer cores make darker lines and need sharpening more often. Firmer cores make finer lines and last longer between sharpenings. 
- Will Blackwing pencils fit a standard sharpener? 

 Yes. The barrel is a standard pencil diameter. The Blackwing One-Step and Two-Step sharpeners are shaped to produce the long, curved point these pencils are designed around. 
- Why is the eraser rectangular instead of round? 

 The flat eraser slides out of the ferrule so you can extend it as it wears, then replace it when it is gone. It has been Blackwing's signature since the 1930s. 
- What is the Blackwing Foundation? 

 A portion of every purchase funds the Blackwing Foundation, which supports arts and music education in public schools.

Blackwing pencils are ideal for illustrators and writers who prefer a soft, dark line. These Blackwing 602 pencils are crafted from incense cedar wood with a sleek, metallic gray lacquer coating. The unique rectangular pink eraser can be extended as it wears down from use, and also pops out completely from the pencil body for replacement. The eraser is latex free, and replacement erasers are available in a variety of colors. 

Blackwing pencils differ in the softness of the graphite core, which can be felt while writing and drawing. These pencils feature a firm core that is strong and long-lasting while still being darker and smoother than a typical #2 pencil.

These pencils were previously known as Palomino Blackwing Pencils.

## Customer Reviews

- Superb pencils in every...

May 10, 2012 Verified Purchase

Superb pencils in every way... no ifs, no buts. Right up there and beyond with Tombow Mono 100 and Hi-uni. The eraser is a real sleeper...when I'm finished with a PB602 I remove the glued on ferrule and adapt it on to my other quality pencils that are otherwise eraserless. My Eagle Turquoise with a PB602 ferrule/eraser attached is a classy looking dude. Don't ever throw away your ferrules when the pencil is used up.

arnkevin See all my reviews
- I've been painting and...

March 16, 2013 Verified Purchase

I've been painting and drawing for nearly 35 years -- where has this DREAM pencil been hiding? I love both the regular Palomino Blackwing and the Palomino Blackwing 602. I tend to draw continuously on a piece of paper. I find both pencils very smooth and rarely if ever have they stopped my line flow with annoying snags along the pencils path. I have used some pencils in the past that have snagged ever few inches. I mean it when I call these DREAM pencils. Thanks for reintroducing them to the market. :)

23 people found this helpful

- These are wonderful pencils...

November 8, 2011

These are wonderful pencils - incredibly smooth. Like writing with butter!! They are great for both general writing and for sketching/drawing. Well worth the money.

16 people found this helpful

dmerle See all my reviews
- I find the 602 to be...

December 27, 2011

I find the 602 to be harder and less dark than regular Palomino Blackwings. The 602 series are more faithful to the original Eberhart Faber Blackwings in lead content as well as design. I really like these for sketching where I use the darker Blackwing more for shading or life drawing they’re both very smooth pencils. I was surprised that the eraser works very well and is removable on a lot of pencils I find the erasers more of an afterthought and I need to carry a separate one. Over all there a great pencil all the ones I’ve tried had nicely centered lead cores. 

16 people found this helpful

jswope See all my reviews
- Received this after reading...

December 11, 2011 Verified Purchase

Received this after reading much fanfare in the press and blogosphere. The 602 is a well-made quality pencil. Lead centering is near perfect, all pencils in a dozen are perfectly straight, the finish is fantastic and well done, and the erasers actually work well. Who would know you can extend them quite a bit over the life of the pencil. It's a surprise the balance is not affected with the big eraser on end, and the cores are smooth, dark, and hold a point well. Will definitely get more. The only problem is choosing amongst some pretty fantastic stuff like mono 100s and hi-uni's.

14 people found this helpful
